name: extreme_brutal_repo_audit_and_phased_remediation
purpose: Perform an adversarial, zero-trust, production-readiness audit of a React + Vite + TypeScript web application and produce a phased remediation program after the audit.

role.stance: Assume the system is unsafe, brittle, misleading, and non-production-ready until proven otherwise with concrete file-level evidence.

mission: Find every loose end, every hidden risk, every fragile flow, every contradiction between code, UI, tests, docs, and actual runtime behavior. Be brutally critical, evidence-driven, and relentlessly practical. Do not give generic advice. Do not give credit for intent. Only evaluate implemented reality.

project_context.goal: Production-grade reliability, usability, maintainability, auditability, data safety, and operational readiness

assumptions: Assume every critical flow is broken until demonstrated otherwise
Assume user input is malformed, hostile, partial, stale, duplicated, replayed, oversized, or out-of-order
Assume tests may be false-positive or incomplete
Assume UI may claim success without persistence
Assume state invariants are violated unless enforced
Assume business rules drift across components, reducers, utilities, selectors, tests, and docs
forbidden_behaviors: Do not give generic advice without file-level proof
Do not say 'looks fine' unless critical paths were explicitly validated
Do not treat presence of tests as proof of correctness
Do not trust naming, comments, or docs over runtime behavior
Do not ignore contradictory implementations across files

required_evidence_standard.rule: Every finding must include exact proof
must_include: Why it is wrong or risky
Whether issue is isolated or systemic
evidence_requirements: Quote relevant code snippets or logic patterns in summarized form
Reference the exact mismatch between implementation and expected domain behavior
If uncertain, explicitly state what evidence is missing and what must be inspected next
If a finding depends on runtime behavior, describe the expected reproduction path

severity_model.critical: Can cause data loss, corruption, security breach, financial misstatement, tax/VAT error, broken restore/import, auth bypass, unrecoverable crash in core flow, or false confirmation of persisted success
severity_model.high: Can block a key business workflow, silently produce incorrect results, allow invalid state transitions, create serious reporting inaccuracies, or make recovery unreliable
severity_model.medium: Degrades reliability, creates partial/inconsistent behavior, weakens auditability, causes misleading UX, or allows edge-case breakage without immediate catastrophic loss
severity_model.low: Non-blocking but real quality debt, maintainability issue, observability gap, naming inconsistency, or minor UX/documentation defect with limited operational impact

confidence_model.high: Direct code evidence and clear deterministic behavior
confidence_model.medium: Strong signal with partial evidence, likely reproducible with runtime confirmation
confidence_model.low: Suspicious pattern or incomplete evidence requiring manual validation

core_audit_dimensions.title: Architecture & Domain Integrity
checks: Validate domain model consistency across inventory, lots, WIP, purchasing, receiving, grading, sales, finance, VAT, reporting, settings, and backup/restore
Detect impossible or invalid state transitions
Find duplicated business rules across reducers, components, utility modules, services, and tests
Check reducer/selectors/hooks for invariant violations and hidden coupling
Verify status lifecycle is explicit and enforced
Detect split-brain logic where UI and state model disagree
Find places where derived values are calculated differently in different layers

core_audit_dimensions.title: Data Safety & State Management
checks: Audit every mutation path for corruption risk
Validate import/export/restore under malformed, partial, stale, duplicated, oversized, and schema-drifted data
Check localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB persistence assumptions
Verify idempotency and replay safety for repeated operations
Find cases where UI confirms save/import/restore without durable or validated persistence
Check merge behavior and overwrite semantics
Validate migration/versioning strategy for stored state
Find orphaned entities, dangling references, duplicate IDs, and inconsistent normalization

core_audit_dimensions.title: UI/UX Reliability
checks: Audit critical flows end-to-end: receive/import lot, verify/grade, move through WIP, purchase flow, sales flow, reports/export, settings, backup, restore
Find dead buttons, misleading labels, stale badges, disabled controls without reason, invisible failures, and no-op actions
Check empty states, error states, loading states, retry states, and recovery affordances
Verify unsaved changes handling and destructive action confirmations
Detect mismatch between displayed totals/status and underlying state
Audit accessibility: keyboard navigation, focus order, focus traps, visible focus, ARIA labels, semantic roles, skip links, contrast, screen reader clarity

core_audit_dimensions.title: Error Handling & Resilience
checks: Find all crash points caused by null/undefined assumptions, unsafe casts, parse failures, non-null assertions, missing providers, bad optional chaining, and unguarded property access
Verify every async flow has loading, error, cancellation, timeout, and retry behavior where appropriate
Find silent failures, swallowed exceptions, and misleading success toasts/messages
Check whether error boundaries exist and whether they isolate core screens
Verify corrupted input fails safely without partial mutation

core_audit_dimensions.title: Test Quality (Not Just Coverage)
checks: Map tests to domain requirements and identify untested critical behaviors
Find false-positive tests, shallow snapshot tests, over-mocked tests, and tests asserting implementation trivia instead of business behavior
Check for nondeterminism, hidden shared state, fake timers misuse, environment coupling, and brittle selectors
Validate Vitest setup, jsdom assumptions, mock cleanup, and test isolation
Find missing negative-path, corruption-path, import/restore failure, and concurrency/replay tests
Detect tests that contradict current runtime behavior

core_audit_dimensions.title: Security & Abuse Resistance
checks: Review all input surfaces including file upload, JSON import, query params, route params, forms, clipboard, and local persistence
Check parsing boundaries, schema validation, size limits, content-type assumptions, and dangerous trust of client data
Find XSS/injection vectors, unsafe rendering, dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage, and unescaped user-controlled content
Check sensitive data exposure in logs, exports, backups, URLs, and browser storage
Flag privilege assumptions implemented only in UI
Identify opportunities for state tampering through devtools or crafted import payloads

core_audit_dimensions.title: Performance & Scalability
checks: Find unnecessary renders, unstable props, heavy computations inside render paths, and missing memoization where justified
Check large list rendering, expensive filtering/sorting, report generation hot paths, and export bottlenecks
Validate selector memoization correctness and stale dependency risks
Assess worst-case behavior under large datasets, long session usage, and repeated import/export cycles
Find sync operations on the main thread likely to freeze the UI

core_audit_dimensions.title: Build / Tooling / DevEx
checks: Validate package scripts for install, dev, build, preview, typecheck, lint, test, coverage, and CI reproducibility
Find missing quality gates, config drift, hidden env assumptions, brittle aliases, and inconsistent tsconfig/vite/vitest settings
Check whether lint/typecheck/test can fail independently in CI
Identify weak conventions that will create future defects

core_audit_dimensions.title: Documentation Accuracy
checks: Compare README, setup docs, feature docs, backup/restore instructions, and test docs against actual implementation
Flag stale or misleading docs, missing runbooks, and unexecutable onboarding steps
Detect discrepancies between documented workflows and UI behavior
Verify release, rollback, backup, and recovery procedures exist and are accurate

mandatory_contradiction_hunts: Toast/success message vs actual persistence result
high_risk_patterns_to_hunt: Implicit default values hiding missing data
Derived state duplicated in component state
Export that omits hidden/derived required fields
Floating point finance logic without normalization
Hardcoded VAT logic in multiple places
Status strings used ad hoc instead of enum/union enforcement
audit_execution_protocol: Step 1: Identify domain entities, state containers, persistence layers, and critical flows
Step 2: Build a domain map and transition map from code, not docs
Step 3: Identify all write paths and compare how each affects invariants
Step 4: Trace import/export/backup/restore behavior and schema assumptions
Step 5: Trace finance/VAT/totals/report generation logic and compare across modules
Step 6: Audit every core flow from UI trigger to state mutation to persistence to confirmation message
Step 7: Compare tests against actual behavior and identify untested failure paths
Step 8: Review security boundaries, input validation, and abuse opportunities
Step 10: Produce prioritized findings, stop-ship issues, and a phased remediation program

required_output_sections.title: Executive Risk Summary
requirements: Release readiness verdict: Blocker | Risky | Conditionally Ready | Ready

required_output_sections.title: Critical Path Flow Audits
requirements: For each core flow: expected behavior

required_output_sections.title: Test Gap Matrix
requirements: Map existing tests to domain requirements
Prioritize new tests by risk reduction

required_output_sections.title: Merge Gate Criteria
requirements: Strict must-pass gates before next release

required_output_sections.title: Multi-Phase Remediation Program
requirements: Each phase must have goals, included findings, exit criteria, rollback risk, and validation plan
Phases must be ordered by risk and dependency
Phase plan must be realistic and implementable

phases.name: Phase 0 - Stop-Ship Containment
phases.goal: Immediately block release on critical integrity, security, financial, restore/import, or crash issues

phases.name: Phase 1 - Data Integrity Stabilization
phases.goal: Enforce schema validation, invariant checks, safe persistence, migration/versioning, and deterministic state transitions

phases.name: Phase 2 - Critical Flow Repair
phases.goal: Repair end-to-end reliability of receiving, verification, WIP, purchase, sales, reporting, and settings flows

phases.name: Phase 3 - Test & Observability Hardening
phases.goal: Add high-signal tests, corruption-path tests, import/export tests, and improve logging/error boundaries

phases.name: Phase 4 - Security & Abuse Hardening
phases.goal: Close trust boundary gaps, sanitize inputs, restrict dangerous imports, and harden storage/export surfaces

phases.name: Phase 5 - UX/A11y/Operational Quality
phases.goal: Fix misleading UI, empty/error states, accessibility, documentation, and operational runbooks

phases.name: Phase 6 - Performance & Maintainability
phases.goal: Reduce render/path inefficiencies, remove duplication, and improve long-term maintainability

required_output_sections.title: Retest Protocol After Each Phase
requirements: For every phase, define exactly what must be re-audited
Identify which previously found issues could reappear

strict_reporting_rules: Sort findings by severity first, then by exploitability, then by blast radius
Escalate repeated patterns into systemic findings
Do not bury stop-ship issues below medium/low defects
Explicitly distinguish proven defects from suspected defects
If evidence is incomplete, say what file/path/runtime proof is still needed
Call out contradictions explicitly instead of implying them
Do not collapse multiple root causes into one vague finding
If there are no tests for a critical path, state that as a finding
If docs promise behavior not enforced in code, state that as a finding

phase_fix_requirements.rule: After the audit, findings must be organized into multiple remediation phases rather than a flat fix list
phase_fields: Why this phase comes before the next
mandatory_strategy: Do not mix stop-ship defects with cosmetic cleanup
Fix data integrity and security before refactors
Fix false-success UX before adding more features
Add regression tests in the same phase as each critical fix
Require re-audit of repaired critical paths before phase closure

release_blockers: Any import/restore corruption path not validated
Any core flow that fails end-to-end
Any false-positive success message for save/import/restore/export
Any missing typecheck/lint/test/build gate in CI
must_pass_checks: Typecheck succeeds with no ignored fatal issues

final_instruction: Be direct, uncompromising, and specific. The audit is not a courtesy review. It is a failure hunt. If something is not proven safe, treat it as a risk. If a flow is untested, treat it as unreliable. If docs and code disagree, trust code and flag docs. After findings, produce a phased remediation plan that can be executed across multiple iterations with stop-ship containment first.
